questions.explain: Naive full autonomy per region produces policy-level split-brain (e.g., New York scales connection pools up while Singapore scales them down in response to the same cascade); the solution is regional operators for local time-sensitive decisions plus a global policy arbiter (Raft/etcd) with conflict checks for global-scope decisions, and local fallback if the arbiter misses its expiry window.
options: Centralize every decision in one data center
Regional operators act on local time-sensitive decisions without coordination; global-scope decisions go through a global policy arbiter with conflict checks and execution windows
